title: Measles Cases Confirmed in Central New York as U.S. Outbreak Tops 2,000
excerpt: Health officials in Central New York have confirmed new measles cases, adding to a nationwide surge that has now exceeded 2,000 infections across 30 active outbreaks in 2026.
body:
• New measles cases have been confirmed in Central New York, part of a statewide total of 15 cases in 2026, with health departments urging residents to verify their MMR vaccination status.
  • The U.S. has recorded more than 2,030 confirmed measles cases in 2026 across 30 active outbreaks, with 93% of cases linked to outbreak chains and 94% among unvaccinated individuals.
  • New York State health officials are intensifying surveillance and vaccine outreach, particularly as international travel and large events increase transmission risk.
  • Senator Chuck Schumer has demanded the Trump administration rehire fired CDC vaccine experts and restore measles-related grants after Erie County reported its first cases in eight years.

Health officials in Central New York have confirmed new cases of measles in the region, prompting local health departments to launch contact tracing and vaccination outreach efforts. The cases add to New York State's total of 15 confirmed measles infections in 2026 — nine outside New York City and six within the city — as the United States grapples with its worst measles surge in more than three decades.

A National Crisis in Numbers

The CDC has documented more than 2,030 confirmed measles cases across the United States in 2026, surpassing the 2,000 mark for the second consecutive year. Thirty active outbreaks are driving the surge, with 93% of all confirmed cases linked to outbreak chains. The vast majority — 94% — are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

https://x.com/NewsChannel9/status/2088377675064738209

Ongoing outbreaks in Florida, Pennsylvania, Utah, and Virginia remain particularly active, threatening the country's official measles elimination status, a public health milestone achieved in 2000 and maintained for more than two decades. The Pan American Health Organization documented 20,521 confirmed measles cases and 25 deaths across the Americas in the first five months of 2026 alone — a fourfold increase over the same period last year.

"The Trump administration has taken a wrecking ball to programs that keep New Yorkers safe from measles, and Erie County is paying the price."

— Senator Chuck Schumer (D-NY)

New York's Response

The New York State Department of Health has mobilized local health departments to investigate cases and distribute vaccines. Erie County in Western New York reported two cases this summer — its first in eight years — with the county health commissioner warning that unreported cases likely exist.

Senator Schumer has launched a three-pronged push demanding the Trump administration bring back CDC experts fired during government restructuring, restore measles-related grants, and boost funding for public health programs. The senator called the administration's approach "reckless, radical, and rooted in conspiracy, not science."

State health officials are urging all New Yorkers to ensure they have received the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. The CDC recommends two doses — one at 12 to 15 months and another between ages four and six. The first dose is about 93% effective; the second increases protection to 97%.

Travel and Large Events Heighten Risk

The CDC has warned state and local health departments that continued measles transmission, combined with international travel and large events during spring and summer, means additional cases are anticipated. The 2026 FIFA World Cup, held across the United States, Mexico, and Canada this summer, drew more than a million visitors to the New York metropolitan area from countries with active outbreaks.

Mexico, a World Cup co-host, accounted for 10,920 confirmed cases. Guatemala reported 6,209 cases, and Canada had 1,018. Globally, the World Health Organization documented 184,489 measles cases across 155 member states between January and mid-May.

What Diaspora Families Should Know

For Indian-American families, the measles resurgence is a direct concern. Families with frequent international travel — particularly to South Asia, where measles remains endemic — face elevated exposure risk. Health officials recommend that babies six months and older traveling abroad receive an early MMR dose. Adults born outside the United States should verify their vaccination records, as immunization schedules and vaccine availability vary by country.

Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known. The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after an infected person has left a room, and it can be contracted simply by breathing contaminated air or touching infected surfaces.

What's Next

The Central New York cases will be closely monitored as health departments work to contain potential spread. With declining vaccination rates nationally and reduced federal public health funding, epidemiologists warn the U.S. faces a sustained measles threat that could persist well into 2027 without aggressive intervention.
